claims.text: The starting material is bulk HfNbTaTiZr.
Elemental fluctuations can be introduced into bulk HfNbTaTiZr to produce lattice distortion.
Lattice distortion in HfNbTaTiZr will strengthen phonon scattering.
Stronger phonon scattering caused by lattice distortion will reduce the lattice thermal conductivity of HfNbTaTiZr.
HfNbTaTiZr with introduced elemental fluctuations will have a lower lattice contribution to thermal conductivity than unchanged bulk HfNbTaTiZr.
The predicted reduction applies at room temperature.
The prediction is bounded to temperatures from 0 to 200 K.
The exact magnitude of the reduction in lattice thermal conductivity is uncertain.
A comparison of total thermal conductivity between modified and unchanged HfNbTaTiZr can decisively falsify the claimed reduction in the lattice contribution.

contradictions.description: The condition specifies room temperature, conventionally about 300 K, while the stated boundary ends at 200 K.

The outcome concerns the lattice contribution specifically, but the experiment and falsification rule use total thermal conductivity without separating lattice and electronic contributions. A change or lack of change in total conductivity is therefore not decisive for the lattice-specific claim.
